name: bar_global_order
description: Minimal reproduction of the generic block-barrier GLOBAL-store ordering bug. A PHASE-1 (init) writer thread and a PHASE-2 (recursion) writer thread, in DIFFERENT CTA threads, write the SAME global cell out[1] either side of __syncthreads(). On real GPU the BAR.SYNC establishes happens-before so the post-barrier phase-2 write (901.0) wins deterministically; out[1]==901.0 every run. The x86 wrapper runs CTA threads as concurrent std::threads, so if the block barrier does not order phase-separated global stores across it, the phase-1 INIT value (101.0) can win and out[1] is non-deterministic. This is the block-barrier+global-store analog of the warp-membership mass-drop fixed by warp_gather_fix; it is the exact mechanism behind cuDNN compute_alphas_and_betas<float>'s racing alphas[1] cell (alpha[s1][t0] init vs alpha[s0][t1] recursion alias the same flat global index).
build_note: host pins args via ArgAt{0x210..} so default ARG_BASE is irrelevant. Runs the kernel many times to expose the store race.
result_x86: TEST PASSED (out[1]==901.0 every run post-fix; non-deterministic / 101.0 wins pre-fix)
